arguments.explanation: All four parts (u_brown, u_orange, line_green, inverted_u_yellow) were seated at their respective placement frames within each part's registry position and orientation tolerance, confirmed by direct pose query at each place step's close. Each pick-place cycle's grasp was confirmed by contact (force_threshold stop) with final width within grasp_width_tolerance_m, and lift height matched the step's lift_height_m. No in-hand-slip or clamp-effort monitor fired on any of the four held parts. Previously seated parts and base1 (the fixture) stayed within a few millimetres of their prior pose after each subsequent step -- well inside tolerance, and base1 in particular was never acted on and never moved beyond noise-level drift. However, a standing violation remains: during the pick_line_green step, the bystander monitor on hex_red (the other assembly's part, never acted on by any step here) fired, showing hex_red had moved ~0.05m from its run-start pose, exceeding its registry disturbance_tolerance_m of 0.02m. Evidence (get_evidence pose history) shows this as a single-tick jump rather than a gradual drag, and it does not obviously correspond to the commanded robot/part trajectory at that moment (which was operating over 0.5m away); the physical mechanism is not conclusively identified, but the displacement is real, persists to run end (confirmed by a final pose query: hex_red remains at ~0.0645,0.0394 vs its baseline ~0.1145,0.0394), and was never corrected. Per the verdict-selection rule, a standing violation at run end makes this run non_conformant even though the assembly itself completed and every seated part meets its own tolerance.
